title: Browns Pro Bowler Denzel Ward joins Travis Kelce as Cleveland Guardians minority investor
content:
CLEVELAND — Browns cornerback and Northeast Ohio native Denzel Ward is buying into his hometown MLB team, joining fellow NFL star Travis Kelce as a Cleveland Guardians minority investor, multiple industry sources told The Athletic on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly.

The Guardians announced Kelce’s addition to the organization in May and, on Wednesday, the day of the NFL season opener, Ward has followed suit, purchasing a stake in the same minority group.

Ward, 29, grew up in the Cleveland suburb of Macedonia and attended Nordonia High School and Ohio State University. The two-year, $62 million extension Ward received from the Browns in late July should ensure the five-time Pro Bowler plays his entire career with the team that drafted him at No. 4 overall in 2018. Ward has 18 interceptions over 100 career games with the Browns and led the NFL with 19 pass breakups in 2024.

The Guardians’ ownership group is undergoing widespread change. The Dolan family, the longest-tenured owners in franchise history, purchased the team for $323 million in November 1999 after a failed bid to buy the expansion Browns. Four years ago, however, Paul Dolan struck an agreement with David Blitzer to become a minority owner with a pathway for Blitzer to eventually assume controlling interest.

Blitzer’s first option to take over majority control is after the 2027 season, multiple industry sources told The Athletic under condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly. Dolan has insisted he plans to stay on as a minority owner. He’ll have plenty of company, as Blitzer spearheaded the additions of Kelce and Ward. Both players sat in Blitzer’s suite for the Guardians’ home opener in April.

The Guardians had planned to celebrate Kelce’s involvement in June, but the day was rained out. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end instead signed autographs for fans from the players’ parking lot.

Blitzer co-owns the Philadelphia 76ers, who this summer landed their own star with Cleveland roots, as well as the New Jersey Devils, a forthcoming WNBA team and a NASCAR outfit with his business partner Josh Harris, through their venture, Harris Blitzer Sports Entertainment. Blitzer also has ownership stakes in a handful of soccer clubs throughout Europe.

In the spring, Forbes estimated the Guardians’ franchise value to be $1.66 billion, which ranked 26th out of the league’s 30 teams. The Guardians annually carry one of the league’s lowest payrolls.

John Sherman, a Kansas City businessman, originally came aboard as Dolan’s potential successor in 2016, but he divested his shares three years later to instead buy his hometown Royals. After Sherman shifted gears, he and Dolan shopped his stake for several years until they identified Blitzer as the right partner.

In a sit-down interview with The Athletic last summer, Sherman said he “would have made ties (in Cleveland),” but admitted, “It’s just different — to get to do this in your hometown is a pretty special deal, and it’s a rare opportunity.”

Albeit on a smaller scale, Kelce and Ward will get that opportunity.

— Zac Jackson contributed to this report.
